scope: Local Windows diagnostic, not release approval, FPS A/B, Linux/physical-phone parity or energy measurement. Public input hash in timing belongs to pre-final-notes diagnostic inputs; final release gate must measure its own frozen public inputs.

timing.method: Actual generated-engine ABBA: four fresh sequential Windows Chrome SwiftShader mobile contexts CPU x4, four cores/16 GiB hints. A fulfills the unchanged v1.6.302 engine from its preserved bytes; B uses the actual newly generated engine with source-scoped default-loop guard. All other source files identical. Passive setters/sync method timing and 50 ms owned sentinel per actual fence. Eight seconds movement and native auto quality active. CDP CPU profiles filtered to movement. No prototype renderer monkeypatch, pixel-equivalence control or production diagnostic flag.
timing.limitations: Instrumentation costs CPU; setter return time can include driver waiting, not pure CPU/GPU execution. Statistical CPU samples. Not Linux parity, a physical phone, release/FPS A/B or energy measurement.

pixels.method: Same-context fallback/guard/fallback controls, exact every-byte RGBA and dimensions; first actual hardware-desktop result retained from a partial report, plus three remaining results. Identical generated-engine hashes checked. Native detail restoration must finish before capture; desktop imagery full, mobile intentionally boot. No temporal moving-camera pixel-equivalence claim.

sourceReports.excluded: hardware-mobile erroneously waited 45 seconds for full imagery, which native mobile policy intentionally never selects; corrected in remaining run without changing product or gate deadlines.

pixels.rejectedExploration: Original canvas-resize-pixels-2026-10-09 captured before native navigation-quality restoration; raw guard equality failed while later screenshots were identical. Original report/source/images retained externally and not accepted. Stronger phase/quality-state requirements preserve exact pixel equality without tolerance; the original sample did not record the timer and does not prove a unique cause.

cost.runtime: At most one fence per eligible resolution change, one flush, at most 64 timeout-zero polls using only existing default-loop callbacks, then one delete. No extra submitted frames while pending, timers, listeners, network/dependencies or speculative caches. GPU wait remains; native fallback after 1500 ms / 64 polls. Running clocks, first frame, layout/DPR, WebGL1 and public resize remain native.
cost.diagnostic: Four fresh timed startup contexts plus four accepted pixel contexts; earlier failed/exploratory contexts retained. CDP/profile/readback costs local only, raw profiles and screenshots external; no measured RAM/GPU/network/energy saving.
